packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-04: UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading for this packet. My session context included general memory notes about an unrelated manuscript-fragment identification project, but nothing specific to these images. I did nothing beyond the rules: I read PROMPT.md and image-001 to image-026. I also tried to open image-027 to check whether the packet held more images, and that file does not exist. I did not open any other file, search, or listing.

======================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
======================================================================
The packet has two overviews: image-001 (face A) and image-014 (face B). Each overview shows a full opened bifolium, a parchment sheet of about 31 x 23 cm on the scale bar. Each face has two leaves side by side with a central fold. Sewing holes and slits run along the fold, and there is a tear at the lower fold.
- Each leaf has two columns of text, so each face has four columns, about 35 lines per column. The script is a small Gothic book hand with heavy abbreviation, in brown ink, partly faded.
- Red numerals appear at the top of the leaves. They look like running numbers or headers: face A has "ff"(?) on the left leaf and "iiii" plus "xxv"(?) on the right leaf; face B has "ff"(?) on the left and "iiij" plus "xxviii" on the right.
- Two-line enlarged initials alternate red and blue: L, L, L, L, B, I, B on face A and M, L on face B. Red-ink rubric numbers follow the end of sections, e.g. "xxxvi", "xxxvii", "xxxviii l.", "xxxix cap", "v. cap", "vi ca", "xxxv cap". There are also red rubric lines such as "de s(an)c(t)is di[...]". Capitals within the text are touched with red.
- Small marginal letters next to some initials, such as "l" and "b", look like guide letters for the rubricator.
- A later hand wrote a vertical inscription in the left margin of face A, reading "...Voorm...elle, Lampernisse(?) ... Vlie[...]" (uncertain). Face A also has a large ink "9"/"10"(?) between the columns of the left leaf and a cross mark in the lower left margin. Face B has later pencil or ink scribbles in the lower margin.
- A stamp reading "BIBL. UNIV. GENT" appears in the lower margin of both faces. I am reporting the stamp text only and draw no inference from it.
- Damage: faded bands across the middle of each face (fold or water damage), holes, a tear at the lower right of face A's right leaf, and a loss at the left edge of face B's left leaf. Face B's left column (col a) is cut at the left edge, so 1-3 letters are missing from each line start.
- Tentative interpretation: this is continuous narrative prose divided into numbered short chapters. Many units open with "Legitur in vita...", "Beatus ... narrat ...", or "Magister ... narrat ...". I see no commentary or gloss layer and no underlining.

Spans chosen: I read most of every column. The worst areas are the faded middle band of each face (face A col a lines ~18-21, col b ~19-20, col c ~19-20, col d ~13-24) and face A col d generally (very faded, right edge cropped by the photo or trim). Those stay partly unread. A raking-light or UV image of face A col d and of the middle bands would help.

Conventions: (abc) marks an expansion, ? marks an uncertain reading, [illegible] marks unreadable text, and [...] marks loss at a cut edge. Lines are numbered from the top of each column and cited to the tile where I read them best. Tiles overlap, and I list repeated lines only once.

======================================================================

4. LIMITATIONS
======================================================================
- This is an unverified first reading. Many abbreviation expansions are tentative. The highest uncertainty is in the faded middle bands of both faces and throughout face A col d, where large parts are [illegible]. A raking-light or UV image of face A col d would help most.
- Face B col a has lost 1-3 letters at the start of each line (cut edge), so the [...] gaps are physical losses.
- Line numbers count from the top of each column. Tiles overlap: lines repeated across tiles were read once and are cited to the tile where they are clearest.
- Column order within each face is left to right (a, b, c, d) as shown in the overviews. I cannot tell from the images whether the two faces are recto and verso of the same bifolium, or which order the leaves had when bound.
- The red numerals at the top of the leaves are read as visible marks only. I have not interpreted them.
